messages.subject: fitstats
parts:
Hello dear all, I am reading the Kéry and Royle book "Applied Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology" and I am triying to run the island scrub-jay example (p430), but I am having some trouble with the GOF analysis. This is the script

(pb <- parboot(fm1,fitstats, nsim=1000, report=5))
(c.hat <- pb@t0[2] / mean(p...@t.star[,2]))  

When I run it, I have this error

 (pb <- parboot(fm1, fit.stats, nsim=1000, report=5))
Error in match.fun(statistic) : objeto 'fit.stats' no encontrado
 

I have read about the GOF script and I understando that I need to define fitstats, is this correct? 

Thank you very much 

Regards

Antonela

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] fitstats
parts:
Hey Antonella,

have you written fit.stats or fitstats ?

Should be the latter. In any case, in the jay section, we refer to section 7.5.4, where there is a reference to the unmarked function parboot, in the help text of which you find this:

# Function returning three fit-statistics.
fitstats <- function(fm) {
    observed <- getY(fm@data)
    expected <- fitted(fm)
    resids <- residuals(fm)
    sse <- sum(resids^2)
    chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)
    freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2)
    out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)
    return(out)
    }
To avoid problems when there are missing values in your data, you have to add 'na.rm  = TRUE' at some places.

Best regards  --  Marc
